title: The AI says it is fixed
summary: Review an AI-written patch, reject an unsupported claim, and repair the code yourself.

scenario.briefing: An AI colleague submitted a stock patch with a confident message and one passing test. The deployment is waiting on your review. Find the flaw, reject the unsupported claim, and implement a verified fix.

objectives.description: Evaluate the patch against boundary behavior.
Implement and test a correct stock rule.
Explain verification rather than trusting confident output.

hints: Read the comparison. Which quantities does it allow?
Test zero and negative quantities, not just the example in the message.
The claim is unsupported and the function accepts impossible shipments.
Reject the patch, implement both bounds and integer checks, then verify with boundary tests.

misconceptions.description: Treating a confident message as evidence.
misconceptions.feedback: Confidence is not evidence. The function still accepts zero and negative quantities.

misconceptions.description: Accepting one passing example as complete verification.
misconceptions.feedback: One example tests one path. Boundary and invalid cases are where this patch fails.

sections.title: Review the change, not the tone
sections.body: AI messages often sound certain regardless of evidence. Review the actual diff, understand what it does, and run tests that challenge the claim. A patch is not correct because it is described as correct.

sections.title: Verification is a separate skill
sections.body: Delegation is legitimate. Unverified delegation is the problem. Decide what evidence would be sufficient for the risk, gather it, and only then accept the change. For a stock rule, valid boundaries and invalid inputs are essential.

vocabulary.definition: A proposed change to source code.
A statement presented without adequate evidence.
Checking work with evidence not supplied by the author.

steps.title: Review the proposed patch
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.

artifact.title: AI colleague patch
artifact.caption: Submitted with the message shown below.

findings.label: The claim rests on one ordinary input.
The function rejects non-numeric values explicitly.

verdicts.label: Reject and repair with complete boundary tests
Ask for a friendlier message and accept

steps.explanation: The rule lacks a lower bound and integer checks. The message's single example does not cover the failing cases.

steps.title: Implement the verified repair
steps.prompt: Edit stock.js. canFulfill(stock, quantity) must accept only whole quantities from 1 through stock, and only nonnegative integer stock. Run the tests.

steps.title: What counts as verification?

statements.label: The reviewer should read the actual change rather than only the summary.
Boundary and invalid inputs are necessary evidence for a range rule.
Confident language increases the correctness of a patch.
The person accepting the change remains responsible for the outcome.

steps.explanation: Verification uses independent evidence. Tone and authority are not evidence.

accessibility.summary: The AI message and patch are text. Findings, verdict, code, and tests are all keyboard accessible.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Space to select findings, arrow keys for the verdict, and Ctrl+Enter to run code tests.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The patch is announced as code. Each test reports its inputs, expected result, and outcome.
